\section[el relevo]{el relevo — the replacement, the handover; the relay}

\label{lesson:ES-C553-relevo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the border, then the Spanish for to become independent.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el relevo}
\textbf{el relevo} — \textquotedblleft{}the replacement, the handover; the relay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Su hija tomó el relevo en la tienda.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Her daughter took over at the shop.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Tomar el relevo} — to take over. In sport, \emph{los relevos} is the relay.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{relevo} is built on \emph{relevar} 'to relieve, to replace' (EtymDB), which comes from Latin \emph{relevāre} 'to lift up, to lighten', built on \emph{levāre} 'to raise' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el relevo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el relevo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el relevo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the border, then the Spanish for to become independent, then say \emph{el relevo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does el relevo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The replacement, the handover; the relay\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[el ascenso]{el ascenso — the promotion; the climb}

\label{lesson:ES-C553-ascenso}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to become independent, then the Spanish for the replacement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el ascenso}
\textbf{el ascenso} — \textquotedblleft{}the promotion; the climb\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Le dieron un ascenso en enero.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She got a promotion in January.}
\end{quote}

In sport, \emph{el ascenso} is going up a division.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ascenso} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{ascēnsus} 'a going up' (EtymDB), from \emph{ascendere} 'to climb'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to become independent, then the Spanish for the replacement, then say \emph{el ascenso} again
\end{itemize}

\section[el finiquito]{el finiquito — the final settlement, the severance pay}

\label{lesson:ES-C553-finiquito}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the replacement, then the Spanish for the promotion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el finiquito}
\textbf{el finiquito} — \textquotedblleft{}the final settlement, the severance pay\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cobró el finiquito al dejar la empresa.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{He got his final settlement when he left the company.}
\end{quote}

The money owed to a worker when a job ends, and the paper that settles it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{finiquito} is built on \emph{finiquitar} 'to settle an account', usually traced to the old phrase \emph{fin y quito} 'end and quit'. \emph{Fin} comes from Latin \emph{fīnis} 'end'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el finiquito}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el finiquito}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el finiquito}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the replacement, then the Spanish for the promotion, then say \emph{el finiquito} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[despedir]{despedir — to dismiss, to fire; to see off}

\label{lesson:ES-C553-despedir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the promotion, then the Spanish for the final settlement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: despedir}
\textbf{despedir} — \textquotedblleft{}to dismiss, to fire; to see off\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Despidieron a veinte trabajadores.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{They fired twenty workers.}
\end{quote}

It also means to see someone off: \emph{Fuimos a despedirla al aeropuerto.} Stem change: \emph{despido}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{despedir} comes from Latin \emph{dē} and \emph{expetere} 'to ask for, to seek' (EtymDB), built on \emph{petere} 'to seek'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{despedir}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{despedir}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the promotion, then the Spanish for the final settlement, then say \emph{despedir} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[renunciar]{renunciar — to resign, to give up}

\label{lesson:ES-C553-renunciar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the final settlement, then the Spanish for to dismiss.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: renunciar}
\textbf{renunciar} — \textquotedblleft{}to resign, to give up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Renunció a su puesto en marzo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She resigned from her post in March.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Renunciar a algo} — to give something up.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{renunciar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{renūntiāre} 'to report back, to give up' (EtymDB), built on \emph{nūntius} 'a messenger'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the final settlement, then the Spanish for to dismiss, then say \emph{renunciar} again
\end{itemize}
